clauses.reason: Section 1(b): where the Commission, the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense cannot agree whether a permit should issue, the Commission submits the application with the three views to the President for approval or disapproval. Executive Order 12038 section 2(a) (43 FR 4957, effective October 1, 1977 under its section 6) amended the order by deleting 'Federal Power Commission' and 'Commission' wherever they appear in sections 1, 3 and 4 and substituting 'Secretary of Energy' (before: the Federal Power Commission; after: the Secretary of Energy). The procedure continues with the Secretary of Energy and is operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 2 designated the Chairman or Acting Chairman of the Federal Power Commission to sign permits issued under section 1(a)(3). Executive Order 12038 section 2(a) amended Executive Order 10485 'by deleting Section 2 thereof' (held text, 43 FR 4957); the amendment is effective as of October 1, 1977 under section 6 of Executive Order 12038 (the Department of Energy Organization Act's effective date), not on the signing date, February 3, 1978. The actor is the President by Executive Order 12038 and the mechanism is an amendment that deletes the section, so the clause ended on 1977-10-01. The Code prints Executive Order 10485 as amended without a section 2 (CURRENT:EO:10485#0), which confirms the deletion. The inclusive and exclusive readings of the date coincide because the deletion takes effect on that day.

clauses.reason: Section 4 provides that Presidential permits issued under Executive Order 8202 and in force when the order issued, and all permits issued under the order, remain in force until modified or revoked by the President or by the Federal Power Commission. Executive Order 12038 section 2(a) (43 FR 4957, effective October 1, 1977 under its section 6) amended the order by deleting 'Federal Power Commission' and 'Commission' wherever they appear in sections 1, 3 and 4 and substituting 'Secretary of Energy' (before: the Federal Power Commission; after: the Secretary of Energy). The savings of permits has no end date and permits issued under it are still administered (18 CFR 153.1); operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 5 revokes Executive Order No. 8202 of July 13, 1939. The order states no later effective date, so the revocation took effect on its date, September 3, 1953. It is a one-time command whose object, Executive Order 8202, ceased on that date; the Office of the Federal Register catalog note 'Revokes: EO 8202, July 13, 1939' records the same effect. The permits issued under Executive Order 8202 were preserved by section 4, which is a separate clause that continues.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10485 of September 3, 1953 (18 FR 5397; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10485.txt, read in full) designates the Federal Power Commission to receive applications for, and issue, Presidential permits for border facilities for electric energy and natural gas (section 1), lets the Chairman sign them (section 2), authorizes rules (section 3), preserves existing permits (section 4) and revokes Executive Order 8202 (section 5). The held page text of section 1(a)(3) is interrupted by the issue's contents and masthead pages; the packet's 10,449-character machine clause across them is replaced by two clauses and the other machine clauses are kept (inventory override of ten clauses). Own terms: no section has an end date. Later instruments: Executive Order 12038 section 2(a) (43 FR 4957, effective October 1, 1977 under its section 6) deleted section 2 and substituted the Secretary of Energy for the Federal Power Commission in sections 1, 3 and 4; it is recorded as a later event on sections 1, 1(b), 3 and 4 and as the end of section 2. The Office of the Federal Register note 'Revokes: EO 8202, July 13, 1939 | Amended by: EO 12038, February 3, 1978 | See: EO 11423, August 16, 1968; EO 12847, May 17, 1993; EO 13337, April 30, 2004' was reconciled: Executive Order 11423 (as amended by 12847), Executive Order 13337 and Executive Order 13867 (2019) each except facilities covered by Executive Order 10485 from the Secretary of State's permit designation, so they recite this order and neither amend, revoke nor supersede it (Executive Order 13867 revokes Executive Orders 13337 and 11423, not this order). The packet's lead 'cited by number, no change provision located: EO:11062' was not confirmed by a search of the held text of Executive Order 11062 for this order's number. Current law: current-law:usc has 6 hits (15 U.S.C. 717b note printing the order as amended by Executive Order 12038, and other Code references), current-law:ecfr has 10 hits (including 18 CFR 153.1 and 153.15), later-events:ofr_catalog 4 hits; no search shows an ending. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.
